correctness.rationale: For every \(n\ge5\) the upper proof checks all legal simultaneous responses to \(n-1\) probes, identifies the only nonterminal pair {a_t,b_s}, and after its closed-neighborhood expansion distinguishes every candidate in a second round. The lower proof maintains that the belief set contains V or V minus two crossed vertices: with \(n-2\) probes there are two unprobed matching indices and a pair of opposing vertices admitting a common shortest-path response at every probe. Their closed neighborhoods renew the invariant and preserve ambiguity forever. Independent exact belief-state enumeration verifies \(3\le n\le6\), and finite policy/invariant branch checks verify \(5\le n\le7\); these checks corroborate but do not prove the infinite statement.

value.rationale: This is an exact optimization and round-complexity theorem for an unbounded regular bipartite family in a newly introduced adversarial geodesic-feedback game. Perfect-matching deletion changes the optimal resource from n to \(n-1\); the lower invariant is structural, not a routine relabeling of the \(K_{n,n}\) proof, and the two-round adaptive strategy explains how missing edges change information. The exact determination is a meaningful natural family classification, not an arbitrary finite slice or an unsupported downstream claim.
